newsitem.title: UK: Taiwan eases loan and premium rules for insurers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan eases loan and premium rules for insurers.

text.p: Taiwan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) has eased restrictions on non-life insurance companies to allow them to offer long-term loans and flexible insurance rates, according to the China Economic News Service.

Currently non-life insurers can only offer only short-term loans of less than 12 months. The removal of the curb will enable them to compete equally with life insurers to provide loans of over one year, including loans to companies and mortgage loans to property buyers.
MOF officials expect this will inject over NT$30 billion worth of housing loans into the real estate market and create a new source of long-term funds for businesses, according to the report.

The MOF will also scrap existing regulations on unified standards for the commissions non-life insurers pay to agents, brokers, and notaries. This will allow the companies to set the premium rates without government intervention and possibly give more discounts to customers.

MOF officials said if the non-life insurance firms are interested in providing extra-long mortgage loans of 30 years as now being offered by life insurers, the firms can make special applications to the MOF, the news service said.

The service also reported that Fubon Insurance, the largest non-life insurance firm in Taiwan, plans to sharply raise its capital, offer more competitive premium rates and conduct mergers and acquisitions in a bid to expand its market share to 30% from the current 21%.
